newsitem.title: INDIA: India to supply water to all villages by mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: India to supply water to all villages by mid-1997.

text.p: India expects to supply water to all of its villages by the middle of next year, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Monday.

"In India, there has been tremendous progress in the rural water supply coverage, but still about three percent of the rural population living in about 72,000 habitations is not covered," he told a world conference on water and sanitation.
"We have resolved to cover these habitations by August 15, 1997--the 50th anniversary of the country's independence," Deve Gowda said.
But he added some 15 percent of India's villages would still be unable to get enough water for their needs.
More than 74 percent of India's estimated population of 930 million live in more than 557,000 villages.
"We have resolved that the entire rural population of the country -- both unserved and underserved -- will be covered by 2000," Deve Gowda said.
He also said the government was working on a law that will regulate the use of ground water resources by preventing a fast depletion of ground water.
Hundreds of people in India die of water borne diseases like cholera every year.
